title: Apple's Not a Trillion-Dollar Stock Anymore

https://www.barrons.com/articles/apples-not-a-trillion-dollar-stock-anymore-1541110314 Apple’s Not a Trillion-Dollar Stock Anymore By Nov. 1, 2018 6:11 p.m. ET Order Reprints Alexandre Godreau / Unsplash Text size
Apple’s (AAPL) market value fell below $1 trillion in after-hours trading after the tech titan offered disappointing guidance for the current quarter.
Apple crossed the $1 trillion mark with much fanfare in August, but the stock was off 7.2%, or $15.92, to $206.30. That put Apple’s value at about $996 billion based on its July 20 share count of 4.83 billion shares.
The market value probably is lower than $996 billion now because Apple has continued to be an aggressive buyer of its own stock, reducing its share count. Apple’s basic share count averaged 4.801 billion shares in its September quarter, which would value the company at about $990 billion. However, the share count probably was below 4.801 billion at the end of the quarter because of ongoing share buybacks that totaled $19.4 billion in the quarter.
Apple bought back $72.7 billion of stock in its fiscal year that ended Sept. 30, a record for any company. Apple has bought back $239 billion of stock since its buyback program began in 2015.
